correctness.rationale: Writing S3=F3⋊F2 turns every word map into sign parity e and F3-linear coefficient arrays c(b), constrained by sum_i(tau_i(b)-1)c_i(b)=tau_e(b)-1. For even-parity words, squares x_i^2 and commutators span each fiber of the kernel: rank k at b=0, k-1 elsewhere. Conjugation supplies multiplication by tau_i, and the character idempotents 2^(-k)prod(1+tau_i(b)tau_i) isolate each b; because 2 is invertible in F3, the actual even-word coefficient arrays realize the entire kernel. Multiplying a fixed parity-e word realizes every solution of the affine identity. Conditional zero-word probabilities are 1 or 1/3 on eligible sign classes and zero elsewhere. Independent closure of all 972 two-variable word functions gave exactly {1/6,1/3,1/2,2/3,5/6,1}, corroborating k=2. All arities follow from the module spanning argument; k=1 uses the actual element order counts in S3.
